Not with Jayson Tatum scoring 40 points and burying a game-winning jumper as overtime expired. But George delivered one of his most complete performances of the young season, helping Boston survive a determined Brooklyn Nets team in a 125-124 victory at TD Garden. Tuesday offered another reminder as the superstar produced 40 points and eight assists without committing a turnover. What Boston needs around him is a collection of players capable of creating offense without making every possession depend on Tatum. item.title: Maryland men’s basketball’s backcourt is filled with impact players
item.description: Pharrel Payne’s return to Maryland men’s basketball will draw the majority of fans’ attention this season — and rightfully so. But the Terps depth lies in the backcourt, with prominent players from the transfer portal and recruiting class pairing up with two returning guards. Head coach Buzz Williams brought in five guards during the offseason to replace Maryland’s departing backcourt production. The new talent has already been showcased in two public exhibition games — the backcourt accounted for 31 of the Terps’ 45 first-half points against Georgia Tech. With half of Maryland’s roster listed as guards, Williams will have several options to choose from on a nightly basis. But that is a good problem for the second-year coach to have. Scoring hinges on Andre Mills In an otherwise disastrous 2025-26 campaign for Maryland, Andre Mills was a bright spot. Mills poured in 12.2 points per game last season, but the majority of that production came after Payne’s season-ending injury. He had double-digit points in 11 of the final 13 games, averaging nearly 18 points per game during that stretch. Mills posted a career-high 39 points against Northwestern, shooting 12-for-17 from the field. But Buzz Williams cited his efficiency as an area of improvement at Big Ten Media Day. “Some of the things that he did for us were incredibly good, but also somewhat inefficient,” Williams said. “But it was because we were asking him to do something that he really wasn’t quite prepared for.” Mills has flashed that efficiency through the two exhibition games. He connected on three of his five first-half shots against Georgia Tech and shot 60% from the field during his 26-point performance to help fuel Maryland’s comeback. While Mills is listed at 6-foot-4, his craftiness and explosiveness around the rim led to some highlight-worthy plays last season. 6-foot-4 Andre Mills goes straight over 7-foot-2 Ivan Njegovan off the dribble. Cue the SportsCenter music. pic.twitter.com/aZJUYig4ot — Testudo Times (@testudotimes) February 6, 2026 That athleticism has helped open up his outside shot; Mills shot 34% from deep last season and knocked down four 3-pointers in the West Virginia exhibition. Mills was asked to do a lot in his redshirt freshman season, operating as the primary ball handler and shouldering much of the scoring load. While he won’t be relied upon to run the offense, Mills likely remains Maryland’s top scoring guard. Fighting for starter minutes Arkansas transfer DJ Wagner will be the team’s lead facilitator and orchestrate the offense this year, joining Mills in the starting backcourt. While Wagner is not a score-first guard — his lone double-digit scoring season came as a sophomore — he provides a level of comfort on the ball that the Terps lacked last season. item.title: ‘Never in a million’ – Pat McAfee reveals 60 Minutes reached out to do a profile amid backlash
item.description: Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images Pat McAfee finds himself in the eye of a media storm and, as a result, has to fend off some of the biggest media outlets in the world. McAfee is arguably the most polarising figure in sports media today, as his loud, abrasive, and brash style of coverage – a style that famously rejects traditional and insightful analysis – has become something many fans have grown tired of. And after a controversial weekend in Utah with the ESPN College GameDay crew, Pat McAfee has taken some strong decisions about his image in the public eye. Pat McAfee vows to boycott ‘all media publications forever’ after 60 Minutes profile request Speaking on his show, Pat McAfee revealed that CBS’ investigative news show, 60 Minutes, reached out to him to do a profile piece on him. McAfee, who was already frustrated after a difficult weekend at the University of Utah, boldly declared that he would not sit down with any media publication going forward. McAfee said: “60 Minutes reached out; they wanted to do a piece — yeah, the f*** right. Yeah, right. Never in a million [years]… Yeah, I’m sure that’d be fair. I’m sure that’d be a-OK. I’m sure that would go great. I would just like to let all media publications (know), I decline. Forever. Thank you. “I’ve read what all of you have had to say, and I really question whether I should be allowed to do anything. I’m just going to continue forging forward, forging the river of sports… That’s literally where I have had to find myself after a lot of ink blots from everybody murdering my every move.” McAfee is clearly feeling the backlash that he has received from media outlets and fans about the nature of his coverage and his overbearing presence on ESPN. The comments he made also suggest that he is feeling frustrated about the way his image is being portrayed by media outlets outside of his partners at ESPN. Clearly, McAfee is starting to push back on the way people perceive him and wants to take control of the narrative. item.title: Mbappé's China row hits Real Madrid and LaLiga; the trouble explained
item.description: Mbappé's China row hits Real Madrid and LaLiga; the trouble explained The diplomatic crisis sparked by Kylian Mbappé in China looks set to extend beyond the player's personal losses, with at least three of his sponsorship deals with Asian brands already going up in smoke. Real Madrid, his current club, and LaLiga, the organization that runs Spain's top-flight league, are also concerned about the potential collateral damage from the controversy. The outrage among the Chinese public stemmed from a lighthearted moment during an interview with the forward and his club and national teammate, Aurélien Tchouaméni, posted on YouTube. Asked about his favorite meme featuring his own image, Mbappé laughed and said he loved an edited picture showing his face on the body of "a Chinese dictator." The subject of the joke, however, was Mao Zedong, the historic founder of the People's Republic of China, who ruled from 1949 to 1976. Although the conversation was originally published in March, the issue only blew up this week after clips went viral on Asian social media. Dongqiudi, one of the country's most influential sports news websites, condemned the player's comment, calling it offensive and wholly inappropriate toward Mao Zedong. The situation is compounded by legislation passed by the Chinese government in 2018 that makes defaming the nation's heroes and martyrs a crime. In addition to a flood of criticism on Weibo, the incident prompted an official statement from Beijing. Guo Jiakun, a spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, said that actions or words that offend the Chinese people will always be strongly condemned by society as a whole. The first direct consequence for the French star was a harsh commercial boycott. Three major local companies cut ties with Mbappé: energy drink brand Dongpeng and dairy producers Mengniu and Milkground. In an attempt to limit the damage, the player gave an interview on Tuesday to publicly apologize for the gaffe. LaLiga president Javier Tebas also had to intervene. Concerned about the competition's future in the Asian market, he issued an apology. According to the Spanish press, Tebas stressed that an isolated incident must not tarnish the commercial partnership or harm the dozens of professional clubs and millions of Asian fans of Spanish football. Even so, these steps failed to prevent severe retaliation. Chinese state broadcaster CCTV blocked broadcasts of Real Madrid's Spanish league matches. Meanwhile, content related to the forward, including goals and statements, was banned from the country's digital platforms. Mbappé's account on RedNote, which had amassed more than a million followers, was taken down for allegedly violating community guidelines. Although Real Madrid remained completely silent on the controversy throughout Tuesday, the Madrid club will not emerge unscathed. item.title: ‘Never in a million years’: Pat McAfee done with the media
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Pat McAfee has never been shy about voicing his frustrations with the media, and it sounds like he’s not interested in giving anyone a chance to interview him anytime soon. On Monday, the ESPN star revealed that CBS’ 60 Minutes had reached out about doing a feature on him. But rather than considering it, McAfee scoffed at the idea that the show would treat him fairly and announced that he plans to turn down every media request going forward. McAfee’s Rough Week McAfee made the revelation during the same episode of The Pat McAfee Show in which he ripped the University of Utah following College GameDay ‘s visit to Salt Lake City. The university had shared a video of students poking fun at McAfee ahead of the show, and he fired back on the broadcast , picking against the Utes and telling the crowd that he hoped he would never see them again. On Monday, he said that he felt uncomfortable on campus and even alluded to the death of Charlie Kirk at Utah Valley University. McAfee has also been feuding with The Athletic, which is now owned by The New York Times , taking repeated shots at the outlet from the GameDay set over a column questioning his role on the show. ‘I Decline. Forever.’ Amidst all of that, McAfee made it clear that he had no intention of sitting down with 60 Minutes, or any other media outlet, for that matter. “ 60 Minutes reached out; they wanted to do a piece — yeah, the [expletive] right,” McAfee said, via Awful Announcing . “Yeah, right. Never in a million [years]… Yeah, I’m sure that’d be fair. I’m sure that’d be a-OK. I’m sure that would go great. I would just like to let all media publications (know), I decline. Forever. Thank you.” McAfee also complained that he had been taken out of context and that the media had been “murdering my every move.” “Because I’ve read what all of you have had to say and I really question whether or not I should be allowed to do anything after reading it,” McAfee said. “But I’m just going to continue forging the river of sports and hopefully one day looking back at all of us, we will have done something worth living.” Clearly, McAfee isn’t interested in hearing what anyone else has to say about him right now. item.title: 'Games volunteers will give veterans warm welcome'
item.description: Maureen Levermore volunteered for the Commonwealth Games in the city in 2022 [Maureen Levermore] Two thousand volunteers from across the world are being sought to help with the Invictus Games in Birmingham next July. Up to 550 wounded, injured and unwell service personnel and veterans from 25 nations are due to take part in the tournament, which will run from 10 - 17 July. A quarter of the roles are to be given to residents of Birmingham and the West Midlands, with a further 25% reserved for people from the armed forces community. "It's another major event in Birmingham and it gives us the opportunity to go and support our service personnel and our veterans – give them the welcome they deserve, it's important," said Maureen Levermore from King's Heath. She was a volunteer at the Commonwealth Games in Birmingham in 2022, and was one of 50 people who pulled Ozzy the bull for the opening ceremony, an experience she described as "awesome". "It's a memory that will last forever, and I encourage anyone to go and volunteer," she told BBC Radio WM. Levermore said she would be signing up to volunteer for the Invictus Games [Maureen Levermore] The Birmingham games will mark the biennial event being held in the UK for the first time since its inauguration in London in 2014. It will take place at the National Exhibition Centre and Sandwell Aquatics Centre, where participants will compete in 12 adaptive sports, including pickleball, wheelchair rugby and swimming. Levermore said she would be signing up to volunteer at the Invictus Games. "I chose to volunteer because it gives me the opportunity to give back to the community," Levermore said. "I was born in Birmingham and I still live here, so for me, it gives me that opportunity to give back to our community, it helps me to develop new skills… create lasting friendship and maintain a positive mindset. "It's like a domino effect, you tell your family and friends, and then they tell their family and friends," she added. The Invictus Games take place every two years [Run Communications] Volunteers must be over 18 and available for a suggested five rostered sessions between 10 and 18 July . Applications remain open until 14 December, with volunteers contacted to let them know if they have been successful between February and March. Venue-specific training will be held at the NEC in June, with uniforms provided. Games CEO Helen Helliwell said the volunteers were "the spirit" of every event who "create the moments that competitors, families, friends and spectators remember long after the Games have ended". "As a volunteer, you're not just supporting an event, you'll play a part in someone's recovery journey, and help shape an inclusive, community-driven Games where every interaction matters." item.title: Barcelona view out-of-favour defender’s exit as key to signing reinforcements in January
item.description: Barcelona view out-of-favour defender’s exit as key to signing reinforcements in January The recent defeats to Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid have made it clear that Barcelona desperately need some reinforcements at the back. That is why the upcoming January transfer window is going to be crucial for the club. And in order to crack the market, the club must finalise the future of Alejandro Balde. The left-back is not a part of Hansi Flick’s plans but recent injuries saw him feature in games against PSG and Real Madrid – matches Barcelona eventually lost. Now, as we near the January transfer window, Barcelona have a plan in place for Balde. Barcelona ready to offload Balde According to SPORT , Balde’s exit is viewed as absolutely key to Barcelona being able to strengthen, with the club prepared to sanction a departure provided the terms are right. All eyes on Balde’s future. (Photo by Daniela Porcelli/Getty Images) Flick was clear with the academy graduate at the start of the season that he would not be counted on, yet Balde opted to stay and fight despite offers on the table. Almost three months on, with his progression stalling, all parties now accept that a solution may be needed. The club are open to either a loan or a permanent sale, but only if a big-money offer arrives, as the funds are what would unlock a move for a defensive addition. His agent, Jorge Mendes, has been active, holding talks with clubs in the Premier League and Serie A. Roma are weighing a January loan with an option to buy, Juventus retain an interest, and Liverpool, Manchester United and Tottenham have all made preliminary enquiries. Barcelona’s targets in January Balde must leave to make way for new signings. (Photo by Yasser Bakhsh/Getty Images) As mentioned earlier, any incoming business hinges directly on that outgoing one. Barcelona have revived their interest in Juventus full-back Andrea Cambiaso , valued at around €30 million and contracted until 2029, with his versatility across both flanks appealing to Flick. The Catalans are also keen on Stuttgart’s highly rated young centre-back Finn Jeltsch , though Real Madrid are monitoring him too. Having spent almost everything on attack in the summer, Deco and co. now recognise the defence needs attention. But with FFP constraints biting, Balde’s exit could be very crucial.

item.title: The one star Indianapolis Colts owner ‘doesn’t want to trade’ despite starting rebuild
item.description: Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images It is time for a new era for the Indianapolis Colts after they fired long-serving GM Chris Ballard, but one player might not be going anywhere. Following their loss against the Tennessee Titans in Week 6 of this NFL season, the Indianapolis Colts made a fairly drastic decision. General Manager Chris Ballard had been in his role for the team since 2017, but he was shown the door as a new era is set to begin. Ed Dodds has been named as interim GM for the franchise, and the rebuild is already underway. Multi-time Pro Bowlers like DeForest Buckner and Quenton Nelson have already been moved on to the San Francisco 49ers and the Seattle Seahawks respectively. This had led to speculation about one particular star. Jonathan Taylor one of the stars that Indianapolis Colts want to keep around Running back Jonathan Taylor has been one of the biggest names on the Colts’ roster for the past few years. The 27-year-old is a veteran at this point, he is in his seventh NFL season. And he would naturally be one of the main contenders to be traded considering the direction the franchise is taking. However, it would seem that despite them moving on from other pillars and leaders on this team, the Colts are happy to keep the running back around. “The big name is Jonathan Taylor. My understanding is that the Colts don’t wanna trade Jonathan Taylor,” Schefter said on the Pat McAfee Show. Despite this take, Schefter has also since reported that Indianapolis will entertain trades for the running back. The 27-year-old would certainly generate more value than they have already received in terms of draft capital. The name of the game is creating cap space, and trading him would achieve that too. But if owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon decides she wants to keep hold of the star, then none of that will matter. Initially, PWInsider’s Mike Johnson speculated that her hiatus was due to an illness. Vaquer recently returned from a three-month hiatus during the Aug. 3 edition of RAW. She had been absent from WWE after her WrestleMania 42 match against Liv Morgan. Vaquer lost the Women’s World Championship after 210 days to the 2026 Royal Rumble winner at the Showcase of the Immortals and took a well-deserved break after. She attacked Morgan, who was holding the title, during the Aug. 3 episode of RAW. Vaquer unsuccessfully challenged Morgan for the title a month later during the Sep. 7 episode of RAW. A few days later, WWE shocked the world and had Vaquer win the title back during an untelevised house show in Santiago, Chile. Lynch was the special guest referee of the match. Sadly, her second reign did not last very long. item.title: Fenerbahce appoint former Liverpool star Dirk Kuyt as interim manager after Ismail Kartal resignation
item.description: Fenerbahce appoint former Liverpool star Dirk Kuyt as interim manager after Ismail Kartal resignation Fenerbahce have appointed former Liverpool forward Dirk Kuyt as interim manager following the resignation of Ismail Kartal after a disappointing run of results. The Turkish giants confirmed on Wednesday that the 46-year-old Dutchman would take charge of the first team while the club searches for a permanent replacement. Kartal departed on Tuesday following Fenerbahce’s 2-1 defeat to fierce rivals Galatasaray, which left them fifth in the Turkish Super Lig. The Istanbul derby defeat proved decisive for Kartal, whose fourth spell in charge had come under increasing scrutiny following inconsistent domestic and European performances. Fenerbahce confirmed Kuyt’s appointment in an official statement published on social media. “Following Ismail Kartal’s resignation, our club has appointed Dirk Kuyt as the technical manager of our Football A Team until our new technical director is determined,” the statement read. Kuyt had been serving as Kartal’s assistant since returning to Fenerbahce in June, having previously enjoyed a successful playing career with the Turkish club. The former Netherlands international spent three seasons at Fenerbahce between 2012 and 2015 after leaving Liverpool. He helped the club win the Turkish Super Lig title in 2013-14, alongside domestic cup and Super Cup honours. His familiarity with the club and existing involvement in the coaching setup provide continuity during another period of managerial uncertainty. Kuyt previously spent six years at Liverpool, establishing himself as a popular figure through his work rate and versatility. He made more than 200 Premier League appearances for the Merseyside club and helped them win the League Cup in 2012. After retiring from professional football, Kuyt moved into coaching and initially worked with Feyenoord’s youth teams. His first senior managerial appointment came at ADO Den Haag in 2022, although that spell ended after several months. He subsequently took charge of Belgian side Beerschot in December 2023 and guided them to promotion to the country’s top division. However, his tenure ended in 2025 following a difficult campaign that resulted in relegation. Kuyt later returned to Dutch football with FC Dordrecht before accepting the opportunity to rejoin Fenerbahce as assistant manager. He now faces the challenge of stabilising the team after a difficult start to the season. Kartal’s departure followed a turbulent period that included heavy European defeats and setbacks against domestic rivals. Fenerbahce are expected to continue their search for a permanent head coach while Kuyt oversees first-team preparations. The Dutchman could make his interim managerial debut against Goztepe in the Super Lig, depending on the timing of the club’s next appointment.

item.title: Former Tottenham captain Hugo Lloris hails 'role model' Harry Kane after Ballon d'Or triumph
item.description: TOPSHOT-FBL-AWARD-BALLON D'OR-2026 - AFP Former Tottenham Hotspur goalkeeper Hugo Lloris has paid a glowing tribute to ex-Spurs colleague Harry Kane after the Bayern Munich striker lifted the 2026 Ballon d'Or in London on Monday night. Having shared a dressing room for a decade in north London, the French veteran praised the England captain's complete game and grounded personality. World Cup winner salutes striker Lloris was thrilled to watch his long-time attacking partner claim football's top individual prize alongside the Gerd Muller Trophy at the London Palladium on October 26. Now 33, the Englishman beat Real Madrid star Kylian Mbappe and Barcelona youngster Lamine Yamal to become his country's first winner in 25 years. That accolade followed a 73-goal campaign, a Bundesliga title and a World Cup third-place finish with England. Decade together forged lasting respect After Kane rose through the Spurs ranks in 2009 and completed several loan spells, he became a permanent first-team colleague of Lloris - who arrived in August 2012 - from mid-2013 until joining Bayern in August 2023. The 39-year-old shot-stopper subsequently moved to Los Angeles FC in December 2023. Speaking to L'Equipe , the former France captain lauded his ex-colleague's all-round development: "I'm happy for him. It's great to see a former team-mate win the Ballon d'Or, at home in London. He has an extraordinarily complete skill set, which he has honed season after season. Today, he can do everything: short passes, long passes, tackling, tracking back to defend, and he is undoubtedly the best player in the penalty area." Selfless attitude sets forward apart Unlike many elite stars, the striker never courted media campaigns to boost his credentials, a trait that impressed Lloris deeply as he compared him to previous winners Ousmane Dembele and Karim Benzema. Reflecting on the forward's character and team ethic, Lloris added: "He doesn't chase the limelight. He owes this Ballon d'Or to his sheer professionalism and humility. He is a role model in our sport. "Ousmane Dembele's Ballon d'Or previously rewarded a team-first player, just like Karim Benzema in 2022. Harry is far more than just a goalscoring machine." Domestic cup precedes Klassiker showdown Having already registered 10 goals and seven assists across 12 outings in all competitions this term, Kane will quickly turn his attention back to club matters with Bayern. The Bavarians welcome Magdeburg in the second round of the DFB-Pokal on Wednesday evening looking to advance smoothly. Following that midweek cup tie, they host arch-rivals Borussia Dortmund in a mouth-watering Bundesliga matchday eight clash on Saturday, October 31.

It's the second home of OKC's executive vice president and general manager, who can be seen traversing its many tunnels every game day. item.title: NBA’s Business Is Booming, But Local TV Turbulence Has Cost Teams $450 Million In Revenue
item.description: The NBA season tipped off last week with the league’s 30 teams worth more than $6 billion on average and its business firing on all cylinders. Nowhere was that more evident than the spectacle of opening night, when a showdown between the reigning champion New York Knicks and LeBron James’ Philadelphia 76ers drew average viewership of ​​7.71 million—a record for a prime-time opening night game, and further validation of the NBA’s 11-year, $76 billion broadcast package , which began last season. But while the league’s deals with ABC/ESPN, NBC/Peacock and Amazon Prime Video have meant a windfall—paying out nearly $150 million to each NBA team last season, according to Forbes estimates, up 40% from the final year of the previous television package—the national success has masked a mounting media crisis at the local level. On average, NBA clubs collected roughly $33 million from their local TV rights last season, according to Forbes estimates, down 25% from $44 million in 2024-25. Relative to 2023-24’s average of $48 million, it amounts to a 32% drop—or $453 million in lost revenue across the 30 franchises. The financial blow has not landed equally across the league, however. Sixteen teams that until recently were partnered with the regional sports networks under the FanDuel banner (previously branded as Bally Sports) have been buffeted by the collapse of the RSNs’ parent company (which itself underwent a rebrand from Diamond Sports Group to Main Street Sports Group). Over the course of three years—from the company’s 2023 filing for bankruptcy to 2026, when it began winding down operations in April and officially shuttered in September—the teams have had to scramble to find broadcast homes for their games that don’t make it onto national networks. The hardest hit have been the Dallas Mavericks, whose local TV revenue tumbled 84% from $96 million in 2023-24 to $15 million in 2025-26, but all 16 of the clubs have experienced significant slides—an average of 66%, from roughly $40 million to less than $14 million, according to Forbes estimates. forbes And although an estimated 11 NBA teams have continued to see incremental annual increases in their local TV revenue over the past two years, three clubs are believed to have declined despite having no connection to Main Street: the Utah Jazz, the Portland Trail Blazers and the Knicks, who accepted a 28% reduction in their annual rights fee when MSG Networks, which like the team is controlled by the Dolan family , refinanced more than $800 million in debt in 2025. item.description: Martin Brundle could only praise Max Verstappen 's overtake on Lando Norris at the United States Grand Prix. According to the former Formula 1 driver, the manoeuvre was 'pure Max'. Kimi Antonelli confidently won the United States Grand Prix, but behind the Italian, there was a hard-fought battle for second place. Lando Norris was trying to hold on to second place on older tyres with Verstappen and Charles Leclerc both chasing him. "With fresh tyres Max was inevitably very fast, and it initially appeared that he would be able to make up the extra 20 seconds he must spend in the pitlane for his second stop on Lap 31," Brundle began about Verstappen race at the Circuit of the Americas in his column for Sky Sports. "But he couldn't clear the traffic with much ease. With his radio failing for the second time, but not before he would castigate his team for not moving his team-mate on a different run plan out of the way much sooner, he ended up a fairly disgruntled third." Martin Brundle praised Verstappen's move at COTA - Photo: Race Pictures Martin Brundle praised Verstappen's move at COTA - Photo: Race Pictures Brundle praises Verstappen's overtake on Norris The did not hide his appreciation for Verstappen's move that got him up to second place momentarily. "I did the post-race interviews and Max did though beam a nice smile when I complimented him on his overtake of Lando Norris up into Turn 1. It was pure Verstappen, just as he looked highly likely to lose a position to Leclerc, he converted that into an overtake of the McLaren with a stunning and controlled slice while extremely late on the brakes." In the end, Leclerc managed to get past the former four-time world champion thanks to his fresher tyres. Had there not been a VSC for Valtteri Bottas, Verstappen might have missed out on the podium, given how quickly Lewis Hamilton was closing in on the Dutchman in P4. The Briton crossed the finish line around a second behind the Red Bull Racing driver. Antonelli admits Verstappen's strategy left him concerned in Austin The Italian said that he was "a bit concerned in the beginning" when he saw Verstappen opt for a two-stop strategy last Sunday. He explained : "But we were able to extend and actually the pace came back with the medium, and we were able to extend without losing too much time. So then, as you know, after doing the first stint on the medium, we were like, 'Oh, right, we're going to go for one-stop.' And the hard, to be fair, felt very robust, so I felt pretty confident to go all the way to the end."
